title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 151 (Appointment of director elected by small shareholders)

content.overview: Section 151 provides that a listed company may have one director elected by small shareholders in such manner and on such terms and conditions as may be prescribed. Small shareholders are shareholders holding shares of nominal value of not more than twenty thousand rupees or such other sum as may be prescribed.
content.glance: Listed company may have one director elected by small shareholders (nominal holding ≤ ₹20,000 or prescribed sum) on prescribed conditions.
content.study: A listed company may have one director elected by such small shareholders in such manner and with such terms and conditions as may be prescribed. ‘Small shareholders’ means a shareholder holding shares of nominal value of not more than twenty thousand rupees or such other sum as may be prescribed. The appointment is in addition to other directors and follows the prescribed rules on notice, election, tenure and vacation. Current-law framing: confirm listed company; identify small-shareholder threshold; apply prescribed election conditions.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.body: Applies to listed companies. Permits one director elected by small shareholders.

sections.heading: Small Shareholders
sections.body: Shareholders holding shares of nominal value of not more than twenty thousand rupees or such other sum as may be prescribed.

sections.heading: Prescribed Conditions
sections.body: Manner, terms and conditions of election, tenure and vacation are as prescribed.

provisions.title: Appointment of director elected by small shareholders

examples.title: Listed company election
examples.body: A listed company holds an election of one director by small shareholders under the prescribed rules. Section 151 is engaged.

examples.title: Unlisted company
examples.body: An unlisted private company has no obligation or entitlement under s. 151 to elect a small-shareholders’ director.

hypotheticals.question: Is a small-shareholders’ director mandatory for every listed company?
hypotheticals.analysis: Section 151 is enabling (‘may have’). Whether and how such a director is elected depends on the prescribed conditions and company action.

distinctions.title: Small shareholders’ director (s. 151) vs general appointment (s. 152)
distinctions.left: Optional listed-company director elected by small shareholders
distinctions.right: General appointment of directors by the company in general meeting

misconceptions.trap: Every listed company must have a small-shareholders’ director.
misconceptions.correction: Section 151 is permissive (‘may have’), subject to prescribed conditions.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 151 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm listed company. II. Apply small-shareholder definition. III. Check prescribed election conditions. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Listing status; small-shareholder facts; election process; precise relief.
